title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 129
paragraphs: After Oroetes' wealth had been carried up to Susa, it happened not long afterwards that King Darius, while hunting wild beasts, twisted his foot as he leapt off his horse—and twisted it, it seems, rather violently, for the ball of his ankle was knocked out of its socket. He had been accustomed to keep about him those Egyptians reputed foremost in the art of medicine, and he called on their services now. But by wrenching and forcing the foot they made things steadily worse. For seven days and seven nights Darius could not sleep from the pain he suffered. At last, on the eighth day, when he was in a wretched condition, someone who had earlier, while at Sardis, heard talk of the skill of Demokedes of Croton, reported this to Darius, and he ordered him to be brought into his presence at once. So having found him somewhere unnoticed among the slaves of Oroetes, they brought him forth into the midst, dragging fetters behind him and clothed in rags.
